newsitem.title: USA: PECO sees Pa. substation back by end of Q1.
newsitem.headline: PECO sees Pa. substation back by end of Q1.

text.p: PECO Energy Co said Tuesday it expected the key Whitpain substation in Worcester township, northwest of Philadelphia, to return to full service by the end of the first quarter.
"The word is that by the end of the first quarter," the plant will be back in full service, said company spokesman Michael Wood.
The substation has been running at reduced rates after it was partially damaged by fire in early October.
"It's at limited capacity," Wood said, but declined to give the specific level at which the facility is running.
The Whitpain substation transmits some of the output from the nearby 2,110 megawatt (MW) Limerick nuclear generating complex, which is owned and operated by PECO.
One of the transformers was destroyed in the fire.
"It's a replacement more than a repair," he said.
Some local power market sources speculated replacement work at Whitpain might continue well into spring, citing May as a more likely month for it to resume full service.
During periods of high demand, constraints were imposed to avoid overloading transmission lines running north and east of the Whitpain substation.
